name: Wabi-sabi
eras: roots in 15th-16th century Japan (the tea master Sen no Rikyū); the term entered Western design vocabulary mainly from the 1990s on
garments: not a fashion look — a design and craft philosophy valuing asymmetry, natural materials and visible wear (as in kintsugi, repairing broken pottery with visible gold seams)
reacts_against: symmetry, polish and permanence as ideals, finding beauty in imperfection, asymmetry and the marks of age instead.
revivals: a major 2010s-20s Western interior-design and wellness-marketing trend, sometimes criticized for flattening a specific Japanese philosophical tradition into a beige decorating style

findings: mostly muted — about 90% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from the Aesthetics Wiki images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
